title: ShinkaEvolve: Towards Open-Ended and Sample-Efficient Program Evolution
venue: The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations

publication.venue: The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations

mechanism.domainTask: Open-ended program evolution across mathematical optimization, agent design, competitive programming, and LLM training design
mechanism.populationDetail: Independent program subpopulations are seeded from a shared initial program, evolve in parallel, and occasionally migrate non-best members between islands.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Each island's fixed-size archive preserves multiple evaluated programs under an elite-size constraint; no descriptor-cell archive is described.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Migration is scheduled at configured intervals and protects each island's best program; migration rates and archive sizes vary across task configurations.
mechanism.generationDetail: Diff edits make localized changes, full rewrites broadly modify mutable code while preserving immutable blocks, and crossover combines the primary parent with an additional archive program.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Scalar fitness, public metrics, and textual feedback are stored in the island archive and reused as mutation context; exact outputs vary by domain task.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: An island is first sampled uniformly, then the primary parent is selected within that island by the configured power-law or weighted rule. Crossover adds an additional archive source program.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Code-novelty rejection sampling embeds mutable code, compares it against island programs, and conditionally invokes an LLM novelty judge to reject/resample near-duplicates; this candidate-eligibility mechanism has no dedicated field in the current taxonomy.
